core_obligations: Show the numerical K-theory action is trivial for compactly supported maps.
Use the author geometric mirror and the Deligne groupoid classification of hearts.
Extend agreement from simple objects through all tilts and establish multiplicativity of the retraction.
difficulty_reason: The author relates the double-bubble plumbing to a threefold flopping contraction and uses a classification of bounded hearts by the Deligne groupoid. Compact support forces trivial numerical K-theory action, which identifies the relevant pure braid on simple objects; an induction over tilts extends the identification to every heart and proves the retraction is a homomorphism. This uses a different geometry and heart-classification mechanism from the Milnor and marked-surface results.
